title: Bangles before the son arrives
odia:
ପୁଅ ନାଇଁ, ପୁଅ ପେଟରେ
ପୁଅର ବାପ ଖଡୁ ଗଢଉଚି
ବନମାଳିପୁର ହାଟରେ।
literal_meaning: The son is not here; the son is in the womb. His father is making bangles at Banamalipur market.
meaning_odia: ପୁଅ ଏଯାଏଁ ଜନ୍ମ ହୋଇନାହିଁ, ପେଟରେ ଅଛି; ଅଥଚ ତାହାର ବାପ ବନମାଳିପୁର ହାଟରେ ଖଡ଼ୁ ଗଢ଼ୁଛି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ଆସିବାକୁ ଥିବା ଫଳକୁ ଧରି ଆଗୁଆ ଆୟୋଜନ କରିବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଏହା। ଗର୍ଭସ୍ଥ ପୁଅ ଓ ହାଟରେ ଚାଲିଥିବା କାମକୁ ପାଖାପାଖି ରଖି କଥକ ସେହି ଆଗ୍ରହକୁ ଦେଖାଉଛନ୍ତି। ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତି ମାତ୍ରକୁ ଭୁଲ କିମ୍ବା କୌଣସି ପ୍ରଥାର ପ୍ରମାଣ ବୋଲି ଧରାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
explanation: The son is still in the womb, while his father is already occupied with making bangles at the market. Our editorial reading hears a teasing contrast between an awaited arrival and preparations running ahead of it. The pregnancy is real within the imagined scene; the verse need not condemn every act of preparation before birth.
usage_example: Original imagined example: Before a proposed event is confirmed, an organiser enthusiastically commissions decorative details. A friend recalls the father making bangles while the son is still in the womb.
cultural_context: Banamalipur market supplies a concrete location for the father’s activity, set against the son’s position in the womb. The source names bangles but does not identify their material, intended wearer or a customary occasion for presenting them.
